name: Pirlatapa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only classification comments (Austin 1990); no grammar/phonology of Pirlatapa found.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2001. Karnic classification revisited. In J. Simpson, D. Nash, M. Laughren, P. Austin & B. Alpher (eds), Forty years on: Ken Hale and Australian languages, 245-261. Pacific Linguistics 512. (hdl 1885/254026)
sources.note: p.253, in passing while deriving PK *nhula: '(stress at all stages of Karnic is on the initial syllable of the word)' -- a family-level comparative remark; p.247 explicitly EXCLUDES Pirlatapa from the study 'due to lack of materials' (fn 8: 'The few recorded sentences are thoroughly examined in Austin (1990b)'). Not a statement about Pirlatapa.
Nothing on phonology; cites only Austin 1990 and AUSTLANG L11.

sources.citation: Austin, Peter. 1990. The last words of Pirlatapa. In P. Austin, R.M.W. Dixon, T. Dutton & I. White (eds), Language and history: essays in honour of Luise A. Hercus, 29-48. Pacific Linguistics C-116. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C116.29 (hdl 1885/253724, CC BY-SA online ed. 2015).
sources.note: Nothing. The only linguistic treatment of Pirlatapa: 5 words (Schoknecht 1870s), a few words + 4 sentences (Reuther), Elkin kin terms, and 20 sentences + c.15 words from rememberer Fred Johnson (Hercus tapes NS22/NS23, 18 Jan 1966). No phonology section; only phonological remarks are n.1 p.47 (orthography; vowels a i u, three rhotics) and p.39 (medial apical stop voicing contrast). a full-text search for stress/accent/syllable = 0 hits; read in full.
